encoding_policy.input_encoding: none - the file is bytes. Read binary and decode ISO-8859-1 so every byte round-trips losslessly and no decode can fail (contract C-1.3, C-1.4)
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: full: the landed bytes are identical to the bytes the producer dropped, including CR, 0x80-0xFF and any UTF-8 sequence, which is stored as its individual bytes
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: there is no such thing here - every byte 0x00-0xFF is valid input and is preserved. Nothing is replaced, dropped or substituted

malformed_record_policy.details: Bronze does not interpret records: one row per physical line, raw bytes plus source_file and record_no. Malformation is attributed downstream in p2-custbill-parse. No row is ever NULL; a missing field is the empty string (C-3.6).

empty_input_semantics.details: A zero-byte CUSTBILL*.dat lands and is recorded in ow_tp.bronze.custbill_files with 0 records. It produces no bronze rows and no error, matching the legacy (C-1.6).

acceptance_checks.description: Every CUSTBILL*.dat in the pinned fixture set lands exactly once; bronze row count equals the total physical line count of the inputs.
Landed bytes are identical to the source bytes: per-file SHA-256 of the landed object equals that of the input.
A second run of the unit adds no rows and re-lands no file (file-level exactly-once on the ledger), proven by an actual rerun.
No source file is deleted by the target. The legacy rm is not reproduced.
Landing writes only under /Volumes/ow_tp/bronze/landing/custbill/ and no object outside catalog ow_tp is created.

planted_anomalies.description: The legacy stability check is a 1-second double-stat, so a file still being written can be picked up and parsed. The target lands atomically (staging name + rename), which removes the race.
planted_anomalies.reason: Recon runs against pinned, stable fixtures, so the race cannot be exercised. Behaviour change is recorded as decision P2-D01 and approved at STOP C; it is listed as an unverified path in every recon report.

planted_anomalies.description: The legacy copies to incoming/ and archive/ and then rm's the drop file, swallowing every failure with `|| true`, so a file can be deleted after a failed copy.
/tmp/sftp_ingest.lock is created and never removed, so the lock provides no mutual exclusion and every later run logs 'stale'.
Archive copies are named <file>.<YYYYMMDDHHMMSS>, so two runs in the same second collide and one silently overwrites the other.
planted_anomalies.reason: Sub-second collision is not reproducible in a fixture run. The target replaces timestamp naming with the file ledger, so the collision cannot occur; noted rather than tested.
